title: The Rosamonde telegrams: Sun Yat-sen and Soong Ching-ling, 1915–1916

documents.shelfmark: Diplomatic Archives of the MOFA of Japan, 1.6.1.4-2-1-2 vol. 1, JACAR B03050087600 (8 Jan - 11 Mar 1915)

plaintext.source: Japanese copies of the telegrams with no translation; per the contributor no decipherment exists in the volume or in the literature he checked.

transcription.source: Brice Dudout's edition (bdudout.github.io/wenmi/en/rosamonde.html): forms transcribed from the JACAR scans by Claude and, blind, by Brice Dudout (89% of letters identical in the initial sample).
transcription.notes: Eleven telegrams (17, 20, 21, 23, 25, 26 Feb; 3, 6, 7, 9, 11 Mar 1915). The project transcribed two of them (20 and 26 Feb, images 45 and 52) from the scans in the contributor's repository: 15 ten-letter words, measured in ciphertext_checked.txt together with 7 July. The contributor's full transcription is not in his public repository, so the set's length is not measured here.

documents.shelfmark: Diplomatic Archives of the MOFA of Japan, 1.6.1.4-2-1-2 vol. 1, JACAR B03050087700 (Mar 1915 - Feb 1916)

transcription.notes: Four telegrams (12, 15 Mar; 10 Jun; 7 Jul 1915). The project transcribed 7 July (image 50): 5 words, 50 letters.

documents.shelfmark: Diplomatic Archives of the MOFA of Japan, 1.6.1.4-2-1-2 vol. 3, JACAR B03050089000 (29 Apr - 22 May 1916)

transcription.source: Brice Dudout's edition; per his page the 1916 forms were transcribed blind before the key was found.
transcription.notes: Seven telegrams (1, 4, 8, 10, 11, 12, 13 May 1916). Not checked against the scans here.

system.summary: English telegraphic text, unspaced and cut into ten-letter words, enciphered by a reciprocal letter substitution (twelve swapped pairs, d and p unchanged).
system.notes: Key a-u b-g c-s e-o f-j h-y i-r k-z l-t m-w n-v q-x, d and p fixed; the same key from Feb 1915 to May 1916. Names, numbers, reply addresses and a few words (happy, Inuzuka, iron, trunk) stay in clear. The last word of a message is cut at ten letters (husba[nd]); the 7 July message ends in a stray p. The 1915 forms twice write qq where pp is expected (6 Mar). The project's 200-letter sample has 23 distinct letters (measured).

prior_solution.where: Per the contributor, not in Bourdeau's sunintercepts work on the 1916 intercepts, Yang Tianshi 2001, Zhu Jiulin 2016, or Chang & Halliday 1986; other works not yet checked.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout found the telegrams in the JACAR volumes and directed the work; Claude transcribed the forms, Brice re-transcribed them blind, and the key was recovered by simulated annealing with an English quadgram model (contributor's account). The project only re-deciphered three telegrams from the scans.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Brice Dudout's sessions; he says he mainly uses Opus 5.5)

solution.what: Contributor found a family of ten-letter word telegrams (Tokyo to 'Laisaosang' and 'Rosamonde', Shanghai) among the Chinese-code telegrams in JACAR B03050087600 and B03050087700, and more in the May 1916 volume B03050089000.

Forms transcribed from the 200-dpi JACAR scans twice, by Claude and by Brice Dudout blind (89% of letters identical in the initial 20 texts); the 6 and 7 March 1915 additions reviewed on a prefilled transcription.
Letter index of coincidence 0.062 (natural language, so a substitution, not a code); f and q absent; trigram hea x10.
Simulated annealing over all 26-letter substitutions, then over reciprocal substitutions only, scored by an English quadgram model; key a-u b-g c-s e-o f-j h-y i-r k-z l-t m-w n-v q-x, d p fixed.
English text enciphered with a random key recovered at 100% by the same search.

Out of sample: the key from the 1915 telegrams alone scores the blind 1916 transcriptions at -5.97 against -8.01 +/- 0.27 for 2,000 random reciprocal tables (z = 7.5), and Brice's blind 1915 re-transcription at z = 10.9; a telegram in another system stays at z = 0.6 (contributor's figures).

22 telegrams edited with copyist confusions (n/v, i/r, g/p, a/u, e/c) corrected in brackets; about 45 of 750 letters corrected in the initial 11 complete 1915 telegrams; eight words of 9 Mar 1915, one word of 25 Feb and one group of 7 Jul not read.

Attribution cross-checked: Ching-ling's absence from Japan 28 Oct 1914 - 17 Mar 1915 fits the Tokyo-Shanghai run; Zhu Zhuowen's letters of 2 and 4 Feb 1915 on the relay office fit 'cable to Chu's'; the 9-10 Mar 1915 rumour and the May 1916 iron trunk and Porthos messages agree with Chinese-code telegrams in the same volumes (contributor's account).

Project check: 20 Feb, 26 Feb and 7 Jul 1915 transcribed here from the three JACAR scans in the contributor's repository (20 words, 200 letters) and deciphered with the reciprocal key unchanged (decipher.py). The output agrees letter for letter with the contributor's edition, including his bracketed corrections (toi for tor[t], a for [u], x for [p]ain, e for i[n], b for esca[p]e) and the unread 'xa ins' of 7 July. Two small points: the scan gives abon (g, not p) in '[u]pon', a slip his brackets leave out, and the cipher gives 'soul are mingled' where his edition prints 'souls'.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 200 tokens, 23 types, en-modern order 4: reading -2.435 per letter; random keys -7.545 (z 7.9); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -4.014 (mean -4.315, z 7.4); annealer on the real text -3.456. Verdict: pass.

Retry of the open words on the JACAR scans, 20 Oct 2026: B03050087600 fetched; the 25 Feb form (p. 47, frame 0209) read: ejotrubuvd = of|eliag|and, a garble in the received text; the 9 Mar form not found in frames 0163-0220. Gaps recorded as transmission garbles (blocker illegible).

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): Brice Dudout's readings copied from NOTES.md to texts/readings_dudout.md; the three telegrams transcribed here (ciphertext_checked.txt) re-deciphered with decipher.py to texts/check_decryption.txt; his cipher transcriptions of the other 19 telegrams are not in the repository

Verification 3 (v3_below_b): the 1916 telegrams (B03050089000), scored on the 1916 rows of readings_dudout.md: 0.31 explicit holes, 0.25 plain; 17% of letters are emended look-alikes with no outside text. Demoted to decoded, not read.
Consistency pass (cl): documents[].read for 1916-B03050089000 read -> read in part, matching outcome.texts (decoded, not read) and fraction_read_source.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.435; polyphony 0.0; 0 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -3.456

outcome.method_basis: Per the contributor's page the key was found by simulated annealing over substitutions scored by an English quadgram model, from the cipher words alone, with an enciphered English control; the page names no crib or outside plaintext.
outcome.fraction_read_source: No per-letter reading file in the contributor's public repository. Unread: eight words of 9 Mar 1915, one word of 25 Feb 1915, one group of 7 Jul 1915; the 9 Mar telegram has 30 words.

gaps.item: 9 Mar 1915, eight cipher words in the middle of the 30-word telegram
gaps.detail: Transmission garble on the copy: the contributor checked the form on the scan (15 Oct 2026) and its letters do not decipher under the complete key. Not located here: B03050087600 as downloaded holds frames 0163-0220 and the 9 Mar form was not among those inspected (20 Oct 2026).

gaps.item: 25 Feb 1915, one word after 'throw of[f]', and the end of 'de[vou]t'
gaps.detail: Transmission garble on the copy. Checked here on B03050087600 p. 47 (frame 0209), 20 Oct 2026: the form is clearly written; the word reads ejotrubuvd, deciphering to of|eliag|and, so five letters between 'of' and 'and' are corrupt in what the clerk received. 'de[vou]t' is dogocl on the form: n and a written g and c.
Transmission garble on the copy: the key gives lovesickxa instorture; checked on B03050087700 image 50 here.

gaps.item: May 1916 telegrams (B03050089000): 17% of letters emended from look-alikes, decoded, not read
gaps.detail: transmission and copying confusions on the Japanese copies (n/v, i/r, y/h, g/p ...), as on the 1915 forms checked here; the copies carry no translation, so no outside text can confirm the emended letters

outcome.notes: The reading, transcription and key are Brice Dudout's, made with Claude (Opus 5.5). The identification of sender and recipient rests on cross-checks; no form names them. 'Laisaosang' and Yung's Chinese name are unidentified; 'Chang Ki' (Zhang Ji?) and 'Tai' (Dai Jitao?) are probable.

credits.note: Found the 22 Rosamonde telegrams in the JACAR volumes, recovered the reciprocal key and edited the texts, with Claude (Opus 5.5); agreed on 15 Oct 2026 to cross-posting with attribution and to inclusion in the paper metadata

texts.label: JACAR B03050087600, eleven telegrams, 17 Feb - 11 Mar 1915
texts.summary: Sun Yat-sen in Tokyo to Soong Ching-ling ('Laisaosang' / 'Rosamonde') in Shanghai, Japanese Communications Bureau copies: love telegrams, Yung the rival suitor, 'Reply by cipher ... they can get our secrets by guessing'. Readings are Brice Dudout's (contributed); only the 20 and 26 Feb forms were transcribed and re-deciphered here, his transcriptions of the others are not published.

texts.label: JACAR B03050087700, four telegrams, 12 Mar - 7 Jul 1915
texts.summary: Sun to Ching-ling about her return by the steamer Korea (12 and 15 Mar), 'Are you forgot me?' (10 Jun), and Ching-ling's 'Lovesick ... in torture. Be merciful. Come or free me forever' (7 Jul). Brice Dudout's readings; only the 7 Jul form was transcribed and re-deciphered here.

texts.label: JACAR B03050089000, seven telegrams, 1 - 13 May 1916
texts.summary: Between Shanghai and 'Rosamonde Tokio' after Sun's return to China, May 1916: his safe landing in the French concession, Canton, and repeated orders to leave the iron trunk in Mr Inuzuka's care. Brice Dudout's readings; no cipher transcription of these forms is in the repository.
texts.note: Decoded, not read (v3 check 23 Oct 2026): the seven 1916 readings (Brice Dudout's, texts/readings_dudout.md) score 0.31 on explicit holes, 0.25 plain, hole rate 0.48: 109 of 627 letters (17%) are bracketed, letters the forms give differently (n/v, i/r, y/h, g/p cursive and transmission confusions) and supplied from sense. That is far above the 3% look-alike limit, and nothing outside confirms them: the Japanese copies carry no translation, and no cipher transcription of these forms is in the repository (only Dudout's readings). The sense is plain English and not in doubt in most telegrams, but the letters rest on emendation.
